summary_responses.response: The National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) Board has issued a final rule, effective January 4, 2027, amending its criteria for determining associational common bonds for single associational charters and multiple common bond federal credit unions. Under the new rule, requiring members to purchase a good, product, or service as a condition of membership will no longer automatically disqualify a group from being recognized as an eligible association. While the NCUA preserves its long-standing policy barring groups based primarily on a client-customer relationship, the finalized amendments detail how the agency assesses these relationships with examples and simplify its review process for pre-approved groups. Following the April 2026 proposal, 17 of the 18 public commenters supported the measure—with several requesting clearer definitions and guidelines—while one bankers association opposed it as an erosion of statutory membership restrictions. The Board maintained that the rule falls within its Federal Credit Union Act authority, will enhance consumer access to financial services, and retains existing safeguards to protect the integrity of field of membership requirements.

summary_responses.subtopic: Clearing Agency Capital Management & Securities Exchange Fee Holidays
summary_responses.response: On November 4, 2026, The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) filed an immediately effective proposed rule change with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to implement a clearing fee holiday from December 1 through December 31, 2026. During this period, OCC will reduce its standard $0.025 per-contract clearing fee—and, once it receives all necessary regulatory approvals, its $200 minimum monthly fee—to $0.00 before reverting to the prior schedule on the first trading day of 2027. Continuing a practice used in December 2025, OCC is returning excess capital under its Capital Management Policy because strong 2026 clearing volumes and fewer-than-budgeted months of margin cash interest expenses have pushed its liquid net assets funded by equity (LNAFBE) above 110% of its Target Capital Requirement. Although the fee holiday is expected to result in roughly $77 million in lost revenue, OCC projects it will remain above both its 2026 ($355.3 million) and 2027 ($390.8 million) early warning capital thresholds under realistic volume scenarios. OCC maintains that the fee holiday complies with the Securities Exchange Act by equitably lowering costs while preserving financial stability under Board and SEC oversight, and the Commission has published the notice to solicit public comments.

summary_responses.response: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has announced the updated Medicare Part A inpatient hospital deductible and coinsurance amounts for calendar year 2027, which will take effect on January 1, 2027. For 2027, the inpatient hospital deductible will rise from $1,736 to $1,776, while daily coinsurance rates will increase to $444 for days 61 through 90 of hospitalization, $888 for lifetime reserve days, and $222 for days 21 through 100 in a skilled nursing facility. As mandated by the Social Security Act, CMS calculated the deductible by adjusting the 2026 figure using a 2.32 percent payment-weighted average increase in hospital payment rates and a -0.1 percent real casemix adjustment, with the coinsurance amounts set as fixed statutory percentages of that deductible. Driven by both the higher rates and projected changes in utilization, these updates are estimated to increase total costs to Medicare beneficiaries by approximately $770 million. Finally, because this annual notice simply applies existing statutory formulas rather than establishing or changing a substantive legal standard, CMS waived standard notice-and-comment rulemaking procedures.

summary_responses.subtopic: National Park Administration, Conservation & Multi-Use Trail Regulation
summary_responses.response: Effective December 21, 2026, the National Park Service (NPS) is amending special regulations for Mammoth Cave National Park to expand bicycle access to approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails and permit horseback riding on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road. This final rule implements part of the park's 2024 Comprehensive Land and River Trails Plan and Environmental Assessment, which was developed to modernize deteriorating trails and expand recreational opportunities while protecting natural and cultural resources. Under the updated cycling designations, the park will construct eight new multi-use trails and keep the Mammoth Cave Railroad Bike & Hike Trail and Big Hollow Trail open, while removing bicycle access from the White Oak Trail and closing the Maple Springs Connector Trail for restoration. Additionally, the rule empowers the park superintendent to allow electric bicycles on designated cycling trails and grants a special exception for equestrians to use the lightly trafficked Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road for loop rides and river access. Backed by a December 2024 Finding of No Significant Impact, the NPS will rely on sustainable construction techniques and careful trail alignments to manage erosion, minimize user conflicts, and safeguard sensitive park environments.
